lane.name: Heartland rock
lane.definition: Springsteen, Petty, Mellencamp, Seger: arena-scale American rock that occasionally feeds the V (Nebraska).

albums.label: Columbia
albums.description: The breakthrough Wall of Sound epic that made Springsteen a rock icon, pairing widescreen Spector-style production with sax, glockenspiel and E Street Band bombast on songs about cars, girls and escape. The blueprint for arena heartland rock.
albums.lineage: Grows from the Dylan/Band roots-rock songwriting of V22 into full arena scale, defining the heartland rock lane (X7) that mostly stays outside the Core except for its stripped-down cousin Nebraska.

albums.label: Capitol
albums.description: Seger's commercial breakthrough, blending bar-band rock with nostalgic, plainspoken ballads about growing up in Michigan. The title track's wistful teenage-memory songwriting became a heartland-rock standard.
albums.lineage: Represents the Midwest bar-band wing of X7's arena-rock lineage, staying within classic-rock radio rather than crossing into the Core's DIY scene.

albums.album: Darkness on the Edge of Town
albums.label: Columbia
albums.description: A leaner, angrier follow-up to Born to Run, stripping away strings for harder guitar and working-class fury. Sets up the more austere, character-driven songwriting that Nebraska would push even further.
albums.lineage: Continues the arena-scale storytelling of X7, tightening the sound in a way that anticipates Nebraska's stark turn back toward the Core's folk-songwriting roots.

albums.label: Backstreet/MCA
albums.description: Petty's commercial and critical breakthrough, all chiming Rickenbacker and Telecaster hooks over a tight, radio-ready rhythm section. A defining record of jangly, guitar-forward heartland rock built for classic-rock radio.
albums.lineage: A parallel Southern branch of X7's arena-rock lineage feeding out of the Byrds/Dylan-adjacent jangle of V22, staying in FM-radio rock rather than crossing into Core twang.

albums.label: Capitol
albums.description: Seger's commercial high point, softening his bar-band edge into reflective, radio-friendly ballads about aging and lost youth. It is a polished peak for the Midwest wing of heartland rock, built on piano, warm guitars and his husky rasp.
albums.lineage: Continues the Midwest bar-rock strand of X7, staying firmly on classic-rock radio rather than feeding back into the Core.

albums.label: Columbia
albums.description: A stark, four-track home-recorded album of murder ballads and blue-collar desperation, just acoustic guitar, harmonica and Springsteen's flattened voice. Its bare-bones intimacy became a direct influence on indie and alt-country songwriters decades later.
albums.lineage: The one heartland-rock record that reaches back into the V: its home-recorded, Woody Guthrie-indebted starkness directly influenced alt-country and indie-folk songwriters in V22's Dylan/Band lineage, making it the exception that feeds the Core rather than leading away from it.

albums.label: Columbia
albums.description: The synth-and-drum-machine-inflected blockbuster that made Springsteen a stadium-filling pop icon, its title track's bitter Vietnam-veteran lyric endlessly misread as flag-waving anthem. The commercial peak of 1980s heartland rock.
albums.lineage: Represents heartland rock's full pop-mainstream turn within X7, moving further from the Core's DIY roots than any other Springsteen record here.

albums.label: Riva
albums.description: Mellencamp's farm-crisis record, jangly and hard-hitting guitar rock sung about vanishing small-town Indiana life. It is one of his most explicitly political heartland records, plainspoken and anthemic.
albums.lineage: Sounds like a Midwest counterpart to Springsteen's Nebraska within X7; its small-town storytelling brushes against the Core's songwriting without fully crossing into it.

albums.label: MCA
albums.description: A more ambitious, Dave Stewart-assisted record fusing Southern storytelling with 1980s synth textures, its title track a wistful ballad about Southern identity. Shows heartland rock absorbing the era's production trends.
albums.lineage: Extends the Southern branch of X7 further from its jangle-rock roots into 1980s studio polish, staying outside the Core's rawer sound.
key_tracks: Don't Come Around Here No More
